messages:
alice: Anyone else hit a weird bundle/regression after the latest js-sdk publish? Edge runtime throws 'ReferenceError: exports is not defined' and the client bundle size jumped massively.

benj: Yep, spotted in the sample-app (Next edge). Vendor chunk went from ~400KB -> ~1.8MB. Build log shows runtime referencing "exports" at the top of a supposedly ESM-only bundle.

maya: That usually means our tree-shaker preserved a CJS shim. Are you using any namespace re-exports or mixing import/require? Also check package.json "sideEffects" and the "exports" map.

alice: package.json has: ```"sideEffects": false, "exports": { ".": { "import": "./dist/index.mjs", "require": "./dist/index.cjs" } }``` We bundle with esbuild via the sample-app's build pipeline. Types point to ./dist/index.d.ts. The weird part is Rollup/ESBuild resolving to the cjs path in some cases — I think the bundler is choosing the wrong condition when running under edge (SWC/esbuild interplay?).

sam: I reproduced. Minimal repro: we do `export * from './runtime'` in the top-level index and `runtime` internally does `module.exports = { ... }` historically. During bundling a mixed-ES module got transformed into an interop wrapper that references "exports". Rollup won't tree-shake that if some code does "Object.keys(exports)" or uses a namespace object. Stack trace: ```ReferenceError: exports is not defined at eval (runtime-shim:1:12)```

benj: Also saw TS emit behavior: `export * as runtime from './runtime'` causes TS to emit a namespace import which forces a wider import surface. Type-only re-exports wouldn't, e.g. `export type { Foo } from './types'`.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy failed: /api/generate returned 500 x 85 requests between 2026-03-20T14:22:00Z and 2026-03-20T14:30:00Z.

maya: Quick mitigation options: 1) stop using namespace re-exports that cause require interop, 2) ensure the bundler prefers the "import" condition and resolves ./dist/index.mjs, 3) add a small compatibility ESM wrapper that re-exports only needed symbols instead of exporting the whole namespace. For Rollup/ESBuild: set "conditions": ["import"] in resolution or configure node-resolve plugin to favor "module"/"import".

alice: Proposed patch I can push: - add explicit ./dist/index.mjs that imports tiny pieces from runtime and re-exports named exports (no "export * as ns") - adjust package.json exports so the package root only exposes the mjs for import - update tsconfig to emit "preserveValueImports" where possible - add a test in sample-app to run edge build and assert bundle < 600KB

benj: Also add rollup/esbuild fix: for Rollup add commonjs plugin opts: `{ transformMixedEsModules: true }` and `namedExports` where necessary. For esbuild-based bundlers, ensure "conditions" include "import".

maya: Types note: change broad re-exports to `export type { X } from './types'` or explicit `export { Y } from './runtime'` for values. That avoids TS creating a runtime namespace.

alice: I'll open a PR with the ESM wrapper + exports map change and publish a canary. @maya @benj can you review? I'll attach the build artifact and pre/post bundle size. :thumbsup:

sam: I can smoke test on the Next edge sample and the internal infra microservice. If we get green, we should add a CI check to detect namespace-preserve regressions (bundle size + presence of "exports is not defined").

benj: I'll add a tiny test in devex/fixtures that imports the package via a pure ESM pipeline and asserts no top-level "exports" string in the final bundle and that chunk sizes are under threshold.

alice: Thanks team — landing the canary now, will post results.
